audit_method: Same-agent exact comparison against the frozen source, cited definitions, formal notation, the proof's required constructions and the author-distributed 2019 course PDF where noted. All five corresponding raw files on current official upstream master were also fetched and found byte-identical to the frozen revision.

corrections.finding: The definition says that first-order sentences are built from the constants of the language, omitting its predicate and function symbols.
corrections.handling: Replaced constants by all symbols of the language and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The ordinary inductive definition of first-order formulas uses every nonlogical symbol of the language, and the surrounding clause is defining the full first-order sentence set F(L).

corrections.finding: The renamed structure M-prime is said to correspond to the language L rather than to the original structure M.
corrections.handling: Made M-prime correspond to M and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The same clause already says that L-prime is obtained from L and compares satisfaction in M with satisfaction in M-prime.

corrections.finding: The Quantifier Property places F in L(L), although its displayed model class consists of structures for L-prime after removal of c.
corrections.handling: Placed F in L(L-prime) and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The following display uses Mod indexed by L-prime and explicitly defines L-prime as L without c.

corrections.finding: The text calls partial isomorphism algebraic because it depends only on constants, although its definition also preserves predicates and functions.
corrections.handling: Referred to all nonlogical symbols and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The cited definition of partial isomorphism contains preservation clauses for predicates, functions and constants.

corrections.finding: The proof reuses M for the ambient union structure while M remains one of its internal structures.
corrections.handling: Renamed the ambient structure A throughout the paragraph, figure, caption and subsequent proof, with an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The construction contains M-star and N-star and later refers separately to their internal M and N structures; the 2019 author-distributed course PDF also uses A for the ambient structure here.

corrections.finding: The star following Domain(N) is not placed in exponent position.
corrections.handling: Changed Domain(N)* to Domain(N)^* and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The parallel expression immediately before it is Domain(M)^*, and both denote the starred structures' domains.

corrections.finding: D1 internalizes satisfaction of an arbitrary abstract L-sentence under relativization but is classified as first-order.
corrections.handling: Classified D1 as an L-sentence while retaining D2 as first-order, and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: Relativization and Boolean closure produce an L-sentence; normality then embeds the separately first-order D2 into L so the two can be used jointly.

corrections.finding: The countable ambient model and one of its two internal substructures are both named M-zero.
corrections.handling: Named the ambient countable model A-zero and retained M-zero and N-zero for its internal substructures, with an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The preceding construction distinguishes the ambient structure from the two substructures; the 2019 author-distributed course PDF likewise uses A-zero for the ambient model.

corrections.finding: The proof reuses E, already fixed as the abstract sentence, as the bound first-order sentence in a conjunction.
corrections.handling: Renamed the bound first-order sentence A in both its binder and quantifier-rank condition, with an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The surrounding lemma keeps E fixed while forming D_M from all first-order sentences of bounded quantifier rank.

corrections.finding: The theorem omits normality although its proof invokes the normal-logic properties and its claimed equivalence needs first-order logic to embed into L.
corrections.handling: Restored the normality hypothesis and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The proof uses isomorphism, expansion, Boolean and relativization properties, and the preceding remark obtains the reverse expressiveness inequality only for normal logics.

corrections.finding: After defining M as a union structure, the proof reuses M for a larger coding structure containing M-star, N-star and the natural-number order.
corrections.handling: Renamed the larger coding structure A and updated its later reference, with an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The paragraph must continue to refer to the already-defined M, N, M-star and N-star as components of the new ambient structure; the 2019 author-distributed course PDF also uses A here.

corrections.finding: The sentence D uses ordinary first-order satisfaction symbols for the fixed abstract sentence E.
corrections.handling: Used models-L and not-models-L for E and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: E belongs to L(L), and every surrounding assertion about its truth uses the abstract satisfaction relation models-L.

corrections.finding: Compactness is applied to the single sentence D to assert a nonstandard order element, but D itself has the standard natural-order model and no type forcing such an element is supplied.
corrections.handling: Added a fresh constant c and the finitely satisfiable type saying that at least m elements precede c for every standard m; compactness then yields an ambient model A-star whose c-value is nonstandard. An adjacent keyed note discloses the repair.

mathematical_delta.added: fresh constant c and the type {B_m(c): m in N}

corrections.controlling_evidence: Every finite fragment is realized by placing c sufficiently far along the standard order, while a model of the full type makes c exceed every standard finite predecessor bound. Compactness applies to that set, not to D alone.

rejected_correction_candidates.candidate: Record the phrase 'are build up' as a mathematical source correction.
rejected_correction_candidates.resolution: Rejected: this is an English grammatical typo; the Gujarati renders the intended meaning idiomatically without altering mathematical content.

rejected_correction_candidates.candidate: Correct singular 'disjunction' and duplicated 'can be can shown' through keyed mathematical repairs.
rejected_correction_candidates.resolution: Rejected: both are surface grammar errors and are translated fluently; neither changes a formal claim.

rejected_correction_candidates.candidate: Replace the statement that the Expansion Property comes down to extensionality.
rejected_correction_candidates.resolution: Rejected: although terse, the claim can reasonably describe semantic relevance/locality for first-order sentences and does not create a false step in the chapter's argument.

rejected_correction_candidates.candidate: Treat the proof's assumption of a purely relational language as contradicting earlier vocabulary that also allows functions and constants.
rejected_correction_candidates.resolution: Rejected: this chapter explicitly works in the relational reduction for the back-and-forth theorem; the local restriction is a proof setup rather than an accidental change of the general abstract-logic definition.
